sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Nothing for Mindiri. Mindiri appears only in Proto-Bel sound-correspondence tables, pronoun/possessive tables and a remark on *k retention; its data source is listed as 'Lincoln 1976e Rai Coast Austronesian language survey data, in two parts. Mimeo' with informants 'not recorded'. The book's only stress discussion concerns Ali (Schouten chain), ch. 3.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1976. Austronesian languages: Madang Province. In S.A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 2, 285-299. Pacific Linguistics C-39. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. 4.4.1.1.2.2 defines the Astrolaban Sub-Family (Mindiri, Biliau, Wab) as 'of a rather heterogenous nature'; the 'Note on structure' consists of comparative pronoun/possessive tables with a Mindiri column. No phonology, no stress, no accent mention.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1976. History of research in Austronesian languages: Madang Province. In Wurm (ed.) 1976, vol. 2, 95-114. Pacific Linguistics C-39.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. States that the only published Mindiri material is a 12-item comparative wordlist plus grammatical remarks (possessives 'almost like those in Fijian') in Capell 1962b: 55-56 and Capell 1971: 246, 330, plus Schmitz 1960 ('Mindiri group') and Claassen & McElhanon 1970 wordlists.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Mindiri = language X10 of the Astrolaban Sub-Family, population 93, village Mindiri; the book is a classification/village/population listing with a source-abbreviation table (Mindiri sources: CA, C.M., SC, V.V.). a full-text search for stress/accent: no hits.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Mindiri is not covered (the book treats the Western Madang District; its Belan family = Gedaged, Bilbil, Takia, Megiar, Matukar, Ham). Its general transcription note (ch. 1) says: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.'
